chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymoun, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the feeding of food and the spilling of blood.

key_terms.إِرَاقَةَ: Spilling (specifically of blood in the context of slaughter)

ai.seo_question: What does Allah love regarding food and sacrifice?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the dual concepts of 'it'am al-ta'am' (feeding) and 'irāqat al-dimā' (spilling blood) are highlighted as beloved acts to Allah, with the latter specifically referring to the ritual slaughter for sacrifice (udhiyah) or general charity. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the merit of both daily sustenance provision and the specific ritual of animal sacrifice, linking physical acts of generosity directly to divine pleasure.
